issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong and SUV can run out of gas
issues.sym: The fuel gauge jumps between full and empty, reads empty right after a fill-up, or sticks at one level. The low-fuel light and check engine light may come on, and some owners ran out of gas and stalled in traffic.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor on the pump module inside the tank wears out or gets coated, so it sends wrong readings to the gauge.
issues.next: Until it is fixed, track fuel with the trip odometer and refill early so you never rely on the gauge. A shop usually replaces the sender or the whole fuel pump module.

issues.sym: The low-beam headlights shut off while driving at night, flicker, or will not come back on, while the fog lights and high beams still work.
issues.why: A headlamp driver module can fail and cut power to the low beams. GM recalled many 2006-2009 SUVs on this platform for it (NHTSA 15V-519), though some owners say their VIN was not covered.
issues.next: If the low beams go out, use high beams carefully or fog lights and get off the road safely. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the module replaced.

issues.t: Driver door switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the driver door panel, window and lock switches that stop working, or windows that move by themselves.
issues.why: The driver door switch module can short out and overheat, which can cause a fire even when the SUV is parked. GM recalled these years (NHTSA 12V-406, 13V-248 and 14V-404).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer replace the switch module for free.

issues.t: Door switches stop controlling windows and locks
issues.sym: The driver door switches for windows, locks, mirrors or heated seats stop working, work only sometimes, or the window moves very slowly.
issues.why: The door switch modules and their wiring wear out. A few owners also reported smoke from a door switch.
issues.next: If a switch smokes or smells hot, stop using it and have it checked right away. Otherwise a shop can test the switch and wiring and replace the faulty part.

issues.t: Rear air suspension sags or leaks
issues.sym: The rear of the SUV sits low, leans to one side, bounces over bumps, or takes a long time to rise after starting. A suspension warning may appear.
issues.why: The rear air springs crack and leak with age, or the height sensor, compressor or calibration goes bad. Cold weather makes leaks worse.
issues.next: A sagging rear can affect handling and headlight aim, so avoid heavy loads until it is fixed. Have the air springs, compressor and height sensor checked.

issues.t: AWD binds, hops or howls in tight turns
issues.sym: Jerking, chattering, binding or wheel hop when turning slowly, such as in parking lots, sometimes with a howling noise from underneath.
issues.why: The all-wheel-drive system can bind in tight turns when the front differential or transfer case fluid is worn out or the unit is failing.
issues.next: Have the transfer case and differential fluids checked and changed first. If the binding continues, get the AWD system inspected before it causes more damage.

issues.t: All-wheel drive works only some of the time
issues.sym: A service AWD light or all-wheel drive that seems to cut in and out.
issues.why: Damaged wiring to the transfer case speed sensor can make the system lose its signal.
issues.next: Have a shop check the codes and inspect the transfer case sensor wiring before replacing major parts.

issues.t: StabiliTrak light comes on and engine power drops
issues.sym: The StabiliTrak, traction control or check engine light comes on, and the SUV suddenly slows down or will not accelerate normally.
issues.why: The engine computer cuts power when it sees a fault in the throttle body, a wheel speed sensor or another input to the stability system.
issues.next: If power drops suddenly, move to a safe lane and pull over when you can. Have the codes read; a throttle body or sensor is a common cause.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags deploy without a crash
issues.sym: The side curtain airbags go off while driving or after a small bump, sometimes with the airbag warning light on.
issues.why: Owners have reported side airbags deploying unexpectedly, likely from a fault in the side impact sensors or airbag control system.
issues.next: If the airbag light is on, get the system scanned soon. Check for open recalls on your VIN and have any deployed airbags replaced before driving regularly.

issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, shaking at idle, or rough acceleration.
issues.why: An ignition coil or spark plug fails and a cylinder stops firing properly.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. A coil and plugs are usually the fix.

issues.t: Lifter failure on the V8 causes misfire
issues.sym: A check engine light with a misfire on one cylinder, ticking from the engine, and rough running.
issues.why: The 5.3L V8 uses Active Fuel Management, which shuts off cylinders to save fuel. Its special lifters can stick or collapse.
issues.next: Get a misfire checked quickly. If a lifter has failed, the camshaft may also be damaged, and driving on it can make the repair bigger.

issues.t: Burnt exhaust valve on the inline-six
issues.sym: A misfire and check engine light that will not go away after new plugs and coils, loss of power and rough idle.
issues.why: An exhaust valve can burn and stop sealing, so the cylinder loses compression.
issues.next: Ask the shop for a compression test if a misfire keeps coming back. The cylinder head has to be removed and repaired.

issues.t: Engine shuts off if the key is bumped
issues.sym: A knee or passenger bumps the key and the engine shuts off while driving, or the key gets stuck in the ignition.
issues.why: A worn ignition switch or lock cylinder can move out of Run too easily.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Keep the key ring light and nothing hanging off it. If it has shut off while driving, get the ignition switch and cylinder checked right away.

issues.t: Power steering lines rust through and leak
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid dripping under the front, a whining pump, or steering that gets heavy.
issues.why: The metal power steering lines rust in road salt areas and start leaking.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. If it keeps dropping, replace the leaking line before the pump is damaged from running low.

issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell inside or outside the SUV, sometimes while climbing hills.
issues.why: A fuel or vapor leak somewhere in the fuel system.
issues.next: Treat a gas smell as urgent. Park outside, avoid sparks and flames, and have the fuel system inspected right away.

issues.t: Transmission slips into neutral or the engine cuts out in Drive
issues.sym: The transmission suddenly shifts into neutral at highway speed, or the SUV cuts off while in Drive.
issues.why: Owners have reported this; a dealer cited a software update needed for the transmission controls in one case.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get off the road safely if it happens. Have a dealer check for software updates and transmission codes before driving far.
